Control parameters for nbreg()

nbreg_control.Rd

Tolerances and iteration limits for the three loops used by nbreg(): the outer loop that alternates the two updates, the inner IRLS loop for the regression coefficients, and the inner Newton-Raphson loop for \(\log\theta\).

Usage

nbreg_control(
  tol = 1e-08,
  maxit = 100,
  irls_tol = 1e-10,
  irls_maxit = 100,
  nr_tol = 1e-10,
  nr_maxit = 100,
  theta_max = 1e+08,
  theta_warn = 10000,
  trace = FALSE
)

Arguments

tol

Outer-loop tolerance on the absolute change in the log-likelihood. Default 1e-8.

maxit

Maximum number of outer iterations. Default 100.

irls_tol

IRLS tolerance on the relative change in the log-likelihood. Default 1e-10.

irls_maxit

Maximum number of IRLS iterations per outer iteration. Default 100.

nr_tol

Newton-Raphson tolerance on the absolute step in \(\log\theta\). Default 1e-10.

nr_maxit

Maximum number of Newton-Raphson iterations per outer iteration. Default 100.

theta_max

Upper bound for \(\theta\). Data with no overdispersion push \(\theta\) towards infinity (the Poisson limit); the bound keeps the computations numerically stable. Default 1e8.

theta_warn

A warning is issued when the final \(\hat\theta\) exceeds this value, because the model is then essentially Poisson. Default 1e4.

trace

Logical. If TRUE, print the log-likelihood and \(\theta\) after each outer iteration.

Value

A list of control parameters.

Details

The outer loop stops when the absolute change in the log-likelihood is below tol. The IRLS loop uses the relative change \(|\ell_{new} - \ell_{old}| / (|\ell_{new}| + 0.1)\) < irls_tol. The Newton-Raphson loop stops when the step in \(\log\theta\) is smaller than nr_tol.

See also

nbreg()

Examples

nbreg_control(tol = 1e-10, trace = TRUE)
#> $tol
#> [1] 1e-10
#> 
#> $maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $irls_tol
#> [1] 1e-10
#> 
#> $irls_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $nr_tol
#> [1] 1e-10
#> 
#> $nr_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $theta_max
#> [1] 1e+08
#> 
#> $theta_warn
#> [1] 10000
#> 
#> $trace
#> [1] TRUE
#>
